You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 31d6b4036098f6b59bcfa20375626b500c7d7417 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dany Madden <drt@linux.ibm.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2020 18:04:24 -0600
Subject: [PATCH] ibmvnic: handle inconsistent login with reset

Inconsistent login with the vnicserver is causing the device to be
removed. This does not give the device a chance to recover from error
state. This patch schedules a FATAL reset instead to bring the adapter
up.

Fixes: 032c5e82847a2 ("Driver for IBM System i/p VNIC protocol")
Signed-off-by: Dany Madden <drt@linux.ibm.com>
Signed-off-by: Lijun Pan <ljp@linux.ibm.com>
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>
---
 drivers/net/ethernet/ibm/ibmvnic.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/ibm/ibmvnic.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/ibm/ibmvnic.c
index 2491ebc97871..b28a979061dc 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/ibm/ibmvnic.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/ibm/ibmvnic.c
@@ -4414,7 +4414,7 @@ static int handle_login_rsp(union ibmvnic_crq *login_rsp_crq,
 	     adapter->req_rx_add_queues !=
 	     be32_to_cpu(login_rsp->num_rxadd_subcrqs))) {
 		dev_err(dev, "FATAL: Inconsistent login and login rsp\n");
-		ibmvnic_remove(adapter->vdev);
+		ibmvnic_reset(adapter, VNIC_RESET_FATAL);
 		return -EIO;
 	}
 	size_array = (u64 *)((u8 *)(adapter->login_rsp_buf) +
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The root cause of the bug is an inconsistent login response from the vnicserver, which leads to a mismatch between the expected and actual number of receive add queues during the login process. This inconsistency causes the device to be removed, preventing it from recovering from an error state. The patch addresses this issue by scheduling a fatal reset of the adapter instead of removing it, allowing the device to attempt recovery.

You are a programming expert.
    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.
    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

    
    Provide a response strictly in the following format:
    Code statements:
    <text1>
    <text2>
    <text3>
    <text4>
    ...
    <textN>

Root cause:
The root cause of the bug is an inconsistent login response from the vnicserver, which leads to a mismatch between the expected and actual number of receive add queues during the login process. This inconsistency causes the device to be removed, preventing it from recovering from an error state. The patch addresses this issue by scheduling a fatal reset of the adapter instead of removing it, allowing the device to attempt recovery.
